title: Users, groups, and sudo
subtitle: Identity is the foundation of every permission decision on the system.
objectives: Read the passwd and shadow identity files
Create, modify, lock, and remove user accounts
Grant delegated privilege with sudo and sudoers drop-ins
Explain the difference between su and sudo

commands.desc: Show the current UID, GID, and group memberships.
Query a user through the name service.
Create a user with a home and Bash shell.
Set or change a user password.
Remove a user and home directory. Destructive.
List sudo privileges for the current user.
Safely edit and validate sudoers policy.

lab.title: Provision a least-privilege operator
lab.scenario: Create an account for a junior operator who needs one specific service restart right, not full root.

steps.text: Create a group and a user with a home directory and Bash shell.
steps.cmd: sudo groupadd ops && sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash analyst && sudo passwd analyst
steps.verify: id analyst should show the account and its groups.

steps.text: Add the user to the ops group without removing existing memberships.
steps.cmd: sudo usermod -aG ops analyst && groups analyst
steps.verify: groups analyst should include ops plus every group the account already had.

steps.text: Verify you can query the account through the name service.
steps.verify: getent passwd analyst should return the same entry as /etc/passwd.

steps.text: Create a validated sudoers drop-in granting only the httpd restart command.
steps.cmd: echo "%ops ALL=(ALL) /usr/bin/systemctl restart httpd" | sudo tee /etc/sudoers.d/ops-httpd && sudo chmod 0440 /etc/sudoers.d/ops-httpd
steps.verify: Run sudo visudo -c to validate all sudoers files.

steps.text: Inspect password aging and lock the account when finished.
steps.cmd: sudo chage -l analyst && sudo passwd -l analyst
steps.verify: chage -l should show the aging policy, and passwd -l should add a locked marker.

quiz.q: Which command adds analyst to the engineering group without removing other supplementary groups?
quiz.why: -aG appends. -G alone replaces the supplementary group list and can silently remove access.

quiz.q: Where are password hashes stored on a default RHEL system?
quiz.why: /etc/shadow is restricted to root. /etc/passwd contains an x placeholder in the password field.

quiz.q: Why should sudoers be edited with visudo or a validated drop-in?
options: A syntax error can break privilege escalation
quiz.why: visudo validates syntax before committing. A malformed sudoers file can lock out administrative access.
